# Appeal of Denial — Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-17, Reference Number POC-A389519C6D-33639**
**Member: Quinn Delgado — Member ID: W570305899**
**Governing Policy: Cohere Health: Avera Commercial Guidelines index (Knee Arthroplasty v8, Knee Arthroscopy v10, Hip Arthroplasty v5, Hip Arthroscopy v6, Shoulder Arthroplasty v4, Shoulder Arthroscopy v5, Open Shoulder v4, Cervical Spinal Fusion v5, Lumbar Spinal Fusion v3, Spinal Decompression v4.1, Ankle Arthroplasty v4, Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3) — https://help.coherehealth.com/payer-info/en/articles/13602157-avera-health-plan-commercial-guidelines**

Dear Avera Health Plans Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for bunion surgery (CPT 28296), as stated in the notice referenced above. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision.

My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the record supports that conclusion.

## Why I am appealing

The denial states that this procedure "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," but it does not explain what specific clinical criteria were applied or how my records failed to meet them. The materials I have been given only list document titles from the Avera Commercial Guidelines index — for example, one heading reads "All Collections Review Criteria Avera Health Plan Avera Health Plan:" and another reads "Commercial/Medicaid & Medicare Advantage Guidelines Review Criteria:" — but these are index headings, not the actual clinical standards for great toe/bunion surgery. I have not been shown the specific numbered criteria (such as those that would appear in a "Great Toe Surgical Treatments" guideline) that were used to deny my case, so I cannot yet confirm point-by-point why my treatment was found insufficient. I am not able to quote plan criteria that have not been provided to me, and I want to be direct about that rather than guess at language the plan has not given me.

What I can state plainly is what my own records show, which I believe supports the medical necessity of this surgery:

- **Duration and severity of symptoms:** I have had 18 months of progressive foot pain that is not relieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment already tried and failed:** I completed 12 weeks of physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-04-02 through 2026-06-25), including activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** I used NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04 gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging findings:** Weight-bearing radiographs on 2026-06-07 showed a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- **Functional impact:** I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and there is a documented risk of ulceration over the bony prominence.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **No disqualifying factors:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

Given this history — nearly a year and a half of symptoms, a full course of documented conservative care that did not resolve the problem, objective imaging showing significant deformity, and a functional and skin-integrity risk — I do not understand how this request falls outside medical necessity, and I have not been shown the specific criteria that led to that conclusion.

## Request for the specific criteria used

I am formally requesting, in writing, the exact clinical review criteria applied to deny this request, including the name, edition/version, and relevant section of the guideline used (for example, the applicable version of the "Great Toe Surgical Treatments" guideline referenced in the Avera Commercial Guidelines index). I understand I am entitled to receive this information, and I need it in order to fully respond to the plan's determination.

## What I am asking for

I am asking that Avera Health Plans reconsider this denial and approve coverage for CPT 28296, or, at minimum, provide the specific criteria used so that I and my surgeon can respond directly to any remaining concerns. I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-13** (180 days from the date of the notice). I will send this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is not clear, to the address I am given when I call the member services number on the back of my insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Marchetti's office to complete this review.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Quinn Delgado
Member ID: W570305899
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
